name: QuotaPace
subtitle: Token pace & usage limits
promotional_text: See token usage from local coding logs. Set your own budgets and check an estimate of when you will reach your five-hour limit.
description:
QuotaPace counts tokens from local coding session logs and shows your rolling usage in the menu bar. Choose a supported log folder with the system folder picker. QuotaPace remembers read-only access and refreshes every 30 seconds, without an API key or account connection.

You choose the budgets. In Settings, set a separate token budget for each supported log format and each of the rolling windows, covering the past five hours or seven days, so the displayed percentage uses the allowance you entered. The menu bar shows how much of your five-hour budget you have used. Open Pace details for the average rate and estimated time to your limit, with a forecast that accounts for old usage leaving the rolling window.
 Repeated assistant records are deduplicated, and cumulative counters are counted as changes. A pace estimate needs at least one minute of observed activity and assumes that average pace continues.

These are local estimates against your budgets. Provider billing, shared usage and reset schedules may differ from the logs. Conversations stay in their original files. QuotaPace stores recent counts and timestamps, opaque record identifiers, file counts, refresh times, settings and folder bookmarks in its local container. It sends nothing to the developer.

Disconnect a folder in Settings to remove its permission and cached counts. Sample mode lets you explore the views without your logs, and Launch at Login stays off unless you enable it.

More Mac menu bar apps by Barframe at barframe.com
review_notes:
Launch QuotaPace and click its speedometer menu bar item. Click Try Sample mode (also available as Sample mode in Settings > General). Every usage view works without credentials or private files. Sample data is clearly labeled, uses current timestamps and synthetic usage at millions of tokens per five-hour window.

Select each log format to inspect the five-hour and seven-day totals and percentages. Refresh updates the sample timestamp. Open Pace details to inspect average pace, observed duration, projected usage and time to budget. Open Settings with Settings… or Command-comma. Change either Sample budget and Save; use 1000000 for a reached-limit state, 15000000 for a forecast, or 0 for an unset budget. Invalid values display an error. Exit Sample mode to restore your saved budgets and folder permissions. In live mode, Connect folder uses the system folder picker; Disconnect removes the grant and cache. An empty folder displays the no-usage state. No provider account is accessed in either mode.

General also provides Launch at Login, initially off; pending approval is shown on and can be cancelled by toggling off. About provides Privacy Policy and Support links. Privacy Policy is also in the popover footer. Escape closes the popover; Command-Q quits.

Entitlements. com.apple.security.app-sandbox isolates storage; com.apple.security.files.user-selected.read-only reads only folders chosen with the system picker; com.apple.security.files.bookmarks.app-scope restores those read-only grants after relaunch. No network entitlement or credentials are required.

Screenshots show Sample data in three different features. rolling usage, editable budgets, and pace details. There are no session lists; the usage windows and two supported formats are fixed controls.

With a provisional domain, Privacy Policy and Support open bundled pages inside QuotaPace. Final HTTPS destinations come from the owner-controlled brand configuration. Public hosting and a verified support/privacy contact must be completed before submission.
